questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign. It tells drivers what they must do. This sign is posted near intersections to warn drivers not to block them.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, you should:

options.text: Depend on road signs to find your way.
Only know generally where your destination is.
Always choose the most direct route.

questions.explanation: Plan your trip before you start driving. Check the location on a map. Do not start driving with only a vague idea of where you are going.

questions.question: You may drive around the gates at a railroad crossing:

options.text: When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when you see warning signals. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered crossing gates, a flagger, or a train whistle. Never drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle is fast enough to pass.

questions.explanation: Safe passing requires three things: you can see the road ahead clearly, you can return to your lane before oncoming traffic reaches you, and your vehicle can go fast enough to pass. Only pass when it is legal and safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert you to dangers ahead. This sign tells you that a traffic light is coming up. Be ready to stop for a yellow or red light.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Do all of these things every time you change lanes.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move ahead or fall back so that driver can see you.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection. The light is green but oncoming traffic is heavy. You should:

options.text: Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Take the right-of-way since you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left with heavy oncoming traffic, wait for that traffic to pass. If the light is green and no other vehicle is ahead of you, you can enter the intersection to get ready to turn. Wait for oncoming traffic to clear before turning.

questions.question: Who is required by law to wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?
questions.explanation: In Indiana, all people in a vehicle must wear a seat belt while the vehicle is moving. This applies to everyone in every seat.

questions.question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
questions.explanation: When you see a steady green light, you may continue through the intersection. Yield to any pedestrians in the crosswalk or vehicles still in the intersection. Approach at a speed that lets you slow down or stop if the light changes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be on the road ahead.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Sit in your car and wait for help.
Use your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Sound your horn at passing motorists.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers. Exit the road safely if you can. Move as far from traffic as possible. Lift your hood so drivers know your car is broken down.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead is displaying a red light.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead is displaying a green light.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you there is a traffic signal at the next intersection.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol and drugs while driving can:

options.text: Decrease the effects of the drugs and alcohol.
Increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs together make both effects stronger. Driving after using either one is dangerous. Driving after using both is even more dangerous.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Look both ways before crossing train tracks. Obey all signs and traffic signals. Trains, cars, bicyclists, and pedestrians all share the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They get you ready for road conditions ahead. This sign means the road will soon split into two directions separated by a barrier.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask oncoming drivers to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing against the signal or not paying attention.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Enter above the speed of traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to match the highway speed. Signal before merging. Find an opening in traffic and merge smoothly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that a T intersection is coming up. Be ready to turn left or right.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator sticks while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake.
questions.explanation: Keep your eyes on the road. Shift to neutral right away. Press firmly on the brake. When safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mean no passing zone.

questions.question: Which of these is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep the same speed throughout the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Speed up slowly as you exit. Speeding into a curve makes your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: When can you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.

questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed. Solid lines cannot be crossed, except when you are turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: An upcoming curve in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: An upcoming curve in the road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves to the right ahead.

questions.question: How does night driving compare to day driving?
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. You cannot see as well in the dark. Other vehicles' lights can blind you. More tired and impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: When can you continue through a yellow light?

options.text: There is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane.
You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you can continue through carefully.

questions.question: What should you do when a school bus stops with its stop arm out?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving when you think children are done exiting.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus stops with its stop arm extended. Do not move until the stop arm is pulled in.

questions.question: What must you do if an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street?

options.text: Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until it passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the nearest roadside and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Circular signs warn of railroad crossings. Look for trains and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right.
